 Wp No. 30824 of 2019
 Order

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus and may be pleased to direct the 4th respondent authority to re-determine the market value of schedule portions of schedule A to D properties and to re-consider the order dated 24.03.2017 insofar its relates to Case Nos.LAQ/ARB/NH- 7/15/2012-13, LAQ/ARB/NH-7/16/2012-13,
L A Q / A R B / N H - 7 / 1 7 / 2 0 1 2 - 1 3 , L A Q / A R B / N H - 7 / 1 8 / 2 0 1 2 - 1 3 ,
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/19/2012-13 pertaining to petitioners produced at Annexure- H and grant compensation amount pertaining to acquisition of portions of schedule A to D properties on the basis of prevailing market value as on the date of acquisition in the interest of justice and etc.
2.

Sri K.B. Monesh Kumar, learned counsel appearing for Sri Vijetha R Naik, advocate for petitioners submitted that petitioners were owners of land bearing Sy.nos.72/1 and 72/2 of Kannamangala Village, Kasaba Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, portion of which was notified for acquisition for formation of Hyderabad - Bangalore National Highway-7 under Final Notification dated 17.09.2010 issued under Section 3(D)(1) and (2) of National Highways Act,
1956.
It was submitted that award was passed on 17.08.2011 as per Annexure-G by respondent no.3.
As determination was below market value, petitioner filed application for enhancement of compensation before respondent no.4.

But without proper NC: 2023:KHC:45120 consideration,
respondent no.4 passed order dated 24.03.2017 as per Annexure-H granting inadequate enhancement of compensation from Rs.780/- per square feet to Rs.1,560/- per square feet.
Same was without taking note of relevant documents i.e. sale deeds produced by petitioners in respect of Sy.nos.115, 116 and 117 of Kannamangala Village.

On ground of failure to consider relevant material,
said award was questioned before this Court.
3. On other hand, Sri Yogesh D. Naik, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for respondent no.4 sought to oppose writ petition.
It was submitted that impugned award passed by respondent no.4 at Annexure-H would be an arbitral award as per Section 3(G)(5) of National Highways Act, 1956.

And in case petitioners had any grievance against award, same would be available for redressal only under provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, in view of Section 3(G)(6) of National Highways Act and writ petition for said purpose would not be maintainable,
especially when even said remedy was barred by limitation.
4.
Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.

sentences.text: From above submission, it is seen that petitioners are challenging Annexure-H, which is an order passed by Deputy Commissioner and Arbitrator enhancing compensation under Section 3(G) of National Highways Act.
6. Though award is challenged on ground that respondent no.4 failed to take note of relevant material available, same would be maintainable under Article 226 of Constitution of India.
Petitioners would be required to approach jurisdictional Court under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Writ petition is dismissed, reserving liberty to petitioners to avail remedies under provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, by invoking Section 14 of Limitation Act in case, petitioners are entitled in accordance with law.
